description: Zakat: the obligatory alms, a pillar of Islam, its obligation, conditions (nisab, a year), rate, recipients, Zakat al-Fitr.

documents.text: Zakat is one of the five pillars of Islam. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: "Islam is built upon five: testifying that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establishing the prayer, giving Zakat, Hajj to the House, and fasting in Ramadan." Because it is a pillar, Zakat is an obligatory act of worship for every Muslim who meets its conditions; it is not an optional or voluntary donation.

The Qur'an commands Zakat alongside prayer: "And establish prayer and give zakah and bow with those who bow [in worship and obedience]." (2:43). "And establish prayer and give zakah, and whatever good you put forward for yourselves - you will find it with Allah." (2:110). Zakat is therefore a religious duty (fard) commanded by Allah, mentioned together with prayer many times in the Qur'an.

Zakat on wealth is due only under defined conditions. The wealth must reach a minimum threshold called the nisab, and a full lunar year (hawl) must pass while it is owned. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said that nothing is due on silver until it reaches two hundred dirhams, on which five dirhams are due, and nothing is due on gold until it reaches twenty dinars, on which half a dinar is due, and that no Zakat is due on wealth until a year has passed over it. This corresponds to a rate of 2.5% on qualifying savings, gold and silver. A person whose wealth is below the nisab does not owe Zakat on that wealth.

The Qur'an specifies exactly who may receive Zakat: "Zakah expenditures are only for the poor and for the needy and for those employed to collect [zakah] and for bringing hearts together [for Islam] and for freeing captives [or slaves] and for those in debt and for the cause of Allah and for the [stranded] traveler - an obligation [imposed] by Allah. And Allah is Knowing and Wise." (9:60). Zakat is therefore not given to any cause the giver chooses; it goes to these eight defined categories of recipients. The verse itself calls it an obligation imposed by Allah.

The word Zakat linguistically carries the meanings of purification and growth. The Qur'an says: "Take, [O Muhammad], from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them increase." (9:103). Zakat is understood as purifying the giver's wealth and soul and as a right of the poor in the wealth of those who are able, rather than a favour or a gift.

Zakat al-Fitr is a separate, smaller obligatory charity given at the end of Ramadan before the Eid prayer. Ibn Umar reported that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) enjoined Zakat al-Fitr of one sa' of dates or one sa' of barley upon every Muslim, slave or free, male or female, young or old. It differs from the annual Zakat on wealth.

documents.text: الزكاة ركن من أركان الإسلام الخمسة، وهي فريضة واجبة على كل مسلم ملك النصاب وحال عليه الحول، وليست تبرعاً اختيارياً. قال تعالى: ﴿وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكَاةَ﴾ [البقرة: 43]. وتُصرف الزكاة في ثمانية أصناف حددها القرآن في قوله تعالى: ﴿إِنَّمَا الصَّدَقَاتُ لِلْفُقَرَاءِ وَالْمَسَاكِينِ...﴾ [التوبة: 60]، وختم الآية بقوله: ﴿فَرِيضَةً مِّنَ اللَّهِ﴾.

Contemporary scholars discuss whether and how Zakat applies to new forms of wealth such as digital currencies and company shares. This note is a draft summary of an ongoing discussion and has not yet been reviewed. It must not be used to ground claims in production mode.
